A case is a markdown file with `setup`, `steps` and `expected` (`lynkeus case init` writes an example and the reference). Without files, every case in `cases.dir`. A failed case runs once more before it counts as failed, unless `--once`. `--host` hosts the app in Node for the run.

Arguments

Flags

  --host-heap <percent>    with --host or --keep-hosts: start a host again before a case when its heap is past this percent of its limit (default 60)

  --locale <tag>           the language tag a host the run starts launches with, as in es-AR (default: launch.locale, LYNKEUS_LOCALE)
  --time-zone <zone>       the IANA time zone a host the run starts launches with, as in Europe/Madrid (default: launch.timeZone, LYNKEUS_TIME_ZONE)

  --continue               keep running a case's steps after one fails (a failed setup still stops it)
  --seen <dir>             write <dir>/<case id>.json with the screens each passing case went through, for a coverage map
  --report <file>          append one JSON line per case
  --events <dir>           keep what the app told its analytics, per case, as <dir>/<case id>/events.jsonl
  --out <dir>              write the run as a directory a report can read: run.json and cases.jsonl, a line per attempt
  --no-app-events          with --out: leave the app's own event list unread. Reading it can turn on the app's tracking debug, which may draw on the screen; frames two runs compare should not have it
  --screenshots            with --out: a frame of the screen after every step of the app
  --settle <ms>            with --screenshots: how long the screen must stay still before a frame, in ms; 700 for frames two runs can be compared by (default 150)
  --frames-on-change       with --screenshots: a step that only looks (app.see, app.wait) on an unchanged screen shares the last frame
  --still <ms>             with --screenshots, on a simulator or emulator: take each frame again until two in a row match, this many ms apart (a native transition the agent cannot see)
  --frames <avif|png>      with --screenshots: avif, the default and a few percent of the bytes (a simulator's or emulator's PNG is encoded again), or png, exact, only for frames two runs are compared by pixel for pixel (default avif)

  --traces                 listen for the backend’s OpenTelemetry traces (OTLP over HTTP) and keep, under each step, what the backend did for it; point the backend’s OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT at http://localhost:<traces-port>

  --video-fps <n>          frames per second of the film (default 30)
  --video-scale <n>        pixels per point of the film, where the host takes one (FastSim: 1 to 3, 2 unless told)
  --flakes <file>          the ledger of how each case did across runs (default .lynkeus/flakes.json)
  --prepared <dir>         where `case prepare` leaves setups made ahead; a case found there skips its setup
  --jobs <n>               cases at once, each on its own host (needs --ports) (default 1)
  --ports <list>           the driver port of each job, comma-separated: where its host dials in
  --host-command <command> starts a fresh host for every case and stops it after; {port} is where the host dials, {job} the job

help/fastsim grant:
lynkeus fastsim grant [--platform <ios|android>] [--variant <name>] [--cloud <url>] [--print]

Print a fresh grant a Lynkeus FastSim host needs to start, fetched from lynkeus.io (cached for an hour)

Asks lynkeus.io for a grant for the build this machine runs (--platform ios unless told, or --variant by name) with LYNKEUS_CLOUD_KEY or else the sign-in `lynkeus login` saved, and prints only the grant on stdout when a script reads it (stdout not a terminal, or --print): FastSim's bin/fastsim-run runs `npx --no-install lynkeus fastsim grant --variant <variant>` before each host. At a terminal it prints a summary instead (the variant and until when it is valid), so the token does not sit on screen; --json always carries it. A grant is valid for one hour; it is kept in ~/.cache/lynkeus/fastsim/grants/ (XDG_CACHE_HOME moves it; the file is readable only by you) and reused while it has more than 5 minutes left. Messages go to stderr. It opens a browser to sign in only when stdin and stderr are TTYs and CI is unset; otherwise it exits 2 without a key or a sign-in. Exit code 2 without a key or a sign-in and nobody to ask, 1 when the service refuses (no FastSim entitlement, a key or sign-in it does not accept, or no grants set up) or cannot be reached.

Flags
  --platform <ios|android> the platform it draws: ios or android (default ios)
  --variant <name>         a build by name instead of this machine's (darwin-arm64-ios, linux-x64-android)
  --cloud <url>            service URL (default LYNKEUS_REPORTS_URL or https://lynkeus.io)
  --print                  print the token even at a terminal (it is printed anyway when stdout is a pipe)

Needs: nothing
help/fastsim install:
lynkeus fastsim install [--version <version>] [--platform <ios|android>] [--variant <name>] [--cloud <url>] [--force] [--no-browser]

Download Lynkeus FastSim for this machine and a platform from lynkeus.io with the organization's key

Asks lynkeus.io which Lynkeus FastSim releases the organization may install (with LYNKEUS_CLOUD_KEY, an API key an owner of the organization made with “May download Lynkeus FastSim”, or else the sign-in `lynkeus login` saved, for a member with a FastSim seat; other keys are refused), downloads the build for this machine and --platform (ios unless told: darwin-arm64-ios on an Apple Silicon Mac, linux-x64-android on Linux, and so on; on Windows run it inside WSL2), checks its SHA-256 and its Ed25519 signature (packages are signed by Lynkeus; a release with no signature or a wrong one is refused, nothing is unpacked) and unpacks it into ~/.cache/lynkeus/fastsim/<version>/<variant> (LYNKEUS_FASTSIM_DIR moves it). Install each platform you test on its own: a Mac's iOS build is about 8 MB, its Android build about 65 MB. iOS matches the simulator only on a Mac; on Linux it is close but drawn with another font. An installed release with the same digest is kept. The package's README says how to bundle the app (bin/fastsim-bundle) and run cases on it (bin/fastsim-run with case run --host-command). With no key and no saved sign-in, a person at a terminal (stdin and stderr are TTYs, CI unset) is signed in first, as lynkeus login does, and the install goes on; so is a saved sign-in the service refuses, once. Scripts, CI and MCP never open a browser: they exit 2 and need LYNKEUS_CLOUD_KEY. Exit code 2 without a key or a sign-in and nobody to ask, 1 when the organization has no FastSim entitlement, the machine has no build, or the download fails.

Flags
  --version <version>      release to install (default latest)
  --platform <ios|android> the platform it draws: ios or android (default ios)
  --variant <name>         a build by name instead of this machine's (darwin-arm64-ios, linux-x64-android)
  --cloud <url>            service URL (default LYNKEUS_REPORTS_URL or https://lynkeus.io)

  --no-browser             when a sign-in is needed, print its address instead of opening it

help/mock:
lynkeus mock [route] [--status <code>] [--body <json>] [--delay <ms>] [--times <n>] [--sticky] [--lost] [--hold] [--release] [--clear] [--list]

Answer a request before the network, or hold it until you release it (--hold, --release): a host stands in for the network, on a device the agent does it in the app (--sticky survives a host reset)

With a route and no other flag, the matching requests are answered by a rule (`--status`, `--body`, `--delay`, `--times`, `--lost`). `--hold` is a gate instead: matching requests wait, as far as the app can tell still in flight, so a loading state stays on screen as long as you want; `--release [route]` lets the held ones go on, to a rule or to the network, oldest first, and the gate stays for the next requests (`--times n` holds only the first n). `--clear` drops every rule and gate and lets whatever is held go; so does an app reset on a host, unless the hold is `--sticky`. `--list` also shows what is held and for how long. A held request is not waited for: `idle`, a frame's `--settle` and `clock --settle` go on without it, and `requests` and `clock --settle` report it apart as `held`, outside `inFlight`. Works wherever `--status` does (headless, a device with the agent, Lynkeus FastSim); a host that has no netmock answers `Unknown method`.

Arguments
  route          'GET /path' (a bare path matches any method) (optional)

Flags
  --status <code>          HTTP status to answer (default 200)
  --body <json>            JSON body
  --delay <ms>             answer after
  --times <n>              only this many times
  --sticky                 keep the rule across an app reset
  --lost                   let the request reach the server and fail it on the way back
  --hold                   hold matching requests where they are until --release (the route is required; --times holds only the first n)
  --release                let held requests go on: all of them, or those matching the route
  --clear                  drop every rule and gate, and let held requests go
  --list                   show the rules, the gates and what is held

help/os clock:
lynkeus os clock [--now <iso>] [--advance <ms>] [--reset] [--settle]

Headless and Lynkeus FastSim: what Date answers; --advance runs the timers that fall due; --settle runs what is pending without letting time pass

`--now` and `--reset` change what `Date` answers; timers are not touched. `--advance <ms>` moves the clock forward and runs every timer and interval that falls due inside those milliseconds, in due order, each at its own due time (`Date` answers that instant inside its callback), as `jest.advanceTimersByTime` does: a 5 s `setTimeout` fires on `--advance 5000` and not on `--advance 4000`, with no real waiting. Promise work a timer sets off runs before the next timer. A timer that sets itself again forever inside the window stops the advance after 100,000 runs, with an error that names it. `--advance` answers `advancedMs` (how far the clock moved) and `nextDueMs` (milliseconds until the next timer is due, or `null`). `--settle` runs what is pending now (microtasks, timers due at this instant, queued renders) until nothing is, without waiting for work that is due later, and answers `settled`, `inFlight` (requests still out) and `nextDueMs`; on Lynkeus FastSim `advancedMs` counts what the virtual clock moved in the whole command. `settled: false` means something re-arms itself (an animation loop) and never goes quiet. A Simulator or emulator has no such command: a case step on one is `unsupported`. `idle` is the other way to wait: it lets time pass until the screen is quiet. Combined, the time moves first: `--now`, then `--advance` (firing timers), then `--settle`. A host older than this option moves `Date` and fires nothing: the command fails saying so.

Flags
  --now <iso>              set the time
  --advance <ms>           move the clock forward, running the timers that fall due
  --reset                  back to the real clock
  --settle                 run what is pending to idle without letting time pass (after any of the above)

Needs: the app running with the agent; available in a session; served over MCP
mcp/instructions:
Lynkeus drives a React Native app (bare or Expo) by what is on its screen, and runs cases written as readable steps.

In a project you do not know, call status first: it lists what is set up and, for what is not, the one thing that fixes it.

To set Lynkeus up: call init (it installs lynkeus-agent, mounts it from the app's entry and makes the project's token; nobody sets a variable). The agent has native code, so the app must then be built again (npx react-native run-ios or run-android; npx expo run:ios or run:android, never Expo Go) with Metro restarted with --reset-cache. Do that with your shell if you have one, or ask the person to. Then status until an app is attached.

To write a test: call case_init once if the project has no cases, and read the README.md it writes for the format. Go to the screen with press, type and wait, calling screen to see what is there (press with settle: true answers with the screen once the app has settled; a screen read right after a press can still be the one it left); prefer testIDs (#id) over text. Write the case as a markdown file in the cases folder, then call case_run with that file. A failed step comes back with the screen it failed on: fix the case or report the app's bug, do not weaken the check.

To test without a simulator: call headless_init (it installs what the Node host needs and writes its entry; an Expo Router app works too), then headless_doctor for the native modules still to mock, then case_run with host. The backend the app talks to must be local: set apiUrl in lynkeus.config.json.

To test on Lynkeus FastSim (a simulator that runs the app on a Mac or Linux without Xcode or an emulator, much faster; optional and paid, part of the Team plan, plans at https://lynkeus.io/pricing; use it when the person asks for it or their organization already has it, otherwise the headless host and the Simulator or emulator are free and cover the same cases): fastsim_install with platform ios or android (the sign-in a member with a seat saved by running "lynkeus login" in a terminal, which you cannot do for them: when there is none, tell the person to run it; or, in CI, LYNKEUS_CLOUD_KEY in this server's environment: a key an owner made with "May download Lynkeus FastSim"), then read the README.md in the folder it answers: bin/fastsim-bundle makes the app's bundle, and case_run with host_command set to that folder's bin/fastsim-run <bundle folder> {port} runs each case on its own FastSim host. iOS matches the simulator only on a Mac. When the service refuses (no FastSim in the organization's plan, no seat, a key without "May download Lynkeus FastSim"), tell the person what the refusal says and where to get it (an owner subscribes at https://lynkeus.io/pricing, or gives them a seat under Members), then carry on with headless or the Simulator; never retry with other credentials or look for a way around it.

To share a run: case_run with out, screenshots and push uploads it and prints the report's address. That needs LYNKEUS_REPORTS_KEY in this server's environment.

For a run with everything (frames, film, requests, analytics, backend): case_run with out, screenshots, video (film needs FastSim), traces and push. When the run ends it warns about evidence it could not keep: pass that on.

A case that changes something outside the app (a face enrolled on a shared Simulator) puts it back in `teardown:`, a list of steps with the same syntax as `steps`: it runs after them whether they passed, failed or were skipped, a failing teardown step is only a warning, and a run cut by a timeout never reaches it.
A long case opens each part of its steps with a numbered comment (# 1 Sign in, # 2 A wrong PIN), numbered like its expected list: reports and the live status group the steps by them.

For a long suite: case_run with jobs, ports and host_command runs cases side by side, each on its own host; a case that changes what every case sees (a global flag) declares exclusive: true and runs alone. While a run goes on, case_status says where it is (cases done, what each job runs and in which section, the time left); a client that passes a progress token also hears it as progress notifications.

For a run to repeat exactly (comparing two runs, a time-dependent screen): case_run with seed, locale, time_zone and epoch on a host the run starts (host or host_command). A simulator or emulator that is only attached keeps its own clock and zone; run.json says which facts it could not apply.

A request a case mocked (app.mock) reads (mocked) in requests, trace and a failed case's evidence: it is the case's doing, never the backend's.

To look at a loading state, a case holds the request and releases it later: app.mock with route and hold: true, the steps that look at the screen, then app.mock with release: true. A held request is not waited for (idle and screenshots go on without it) and is reported apart as held, not in inFlight.

Prints a case to finish: the frontmatter with the questions a reader needs answered, the setup the project’s fixtures server offers (from `lynkeus.describe`, commented out: what state the case needs is the author’s call), the presses from --from (default `cases.start`) to the screen as `map plan` knows them, and the checks to write. --write saves it as <cases dir>/<id>.md, never over a file that is there.

mcp/tool/case_run.name: case_run
mcp/tool/case_run.description:
Run cases: setup through fixtures, steps against the app, the evidence when one fails

Runs case files (default: all in cases.dir) against the attached app, or with `host` in Node. A case that fails comes back with its screen and reason. `out` + `screenshots` + `push` uploads the run and prints its address; the report fills case by case from the first. `jobs` runs cases side by side, each on its own host (`ports`, and `host_command` to start one per case); a case with `exclusive: true` in its frontmatter runs alone. With `host`, a host that dies or passes `host_heap` percent of its heap is started again before the next case. `seed`, `locale`, `time_zone` and `epoch` pin the launch facts (a random-value seed, a language tag, an IANA time zone, the instant the clock starts at) on a host the run starts (`host` or `host_command`); on an attached simulator or emulator only the seed applies, and run.json lists the rest under `launch.unsupported`. On Lynkeus FastSim and headless the answer also lists the native values the app read that the host does not know (a constant FastSim answers as true, headless as undefined): each is `Module.name` with a `nativeMocks` snippet to put in the project's cases config, with `value: null` left for you to fill. Work the value out from the library's native code in node_modules (the iOS or Android source that defines the constant, or its Java/Kotlin/Swift/Objective-C `constantsToExport`), then add `{ "value": <json> }`, `{ "ios": …, "android": … }` or `{ "absent": true }` and run again; the same list is `nativeValues` in the run's run.json.

host.description: start `headless start` for the run and stop it after

host_heap.description: with --host or --keep-hosts: start a host again before a case when its heap is past this percent of its limit (default 60)

seed.description: make the random values of the cases repeatable, and tell a host the run starts (default: launch.seed, LYNKEUS_SEED)

locale.description: the language tag a host the run starts launches with, as in es-AR (default: launch.locale, LYNKEUS_LOCALE)

time_zone.description: the IANA time zone a host the run starts launches with, as in Europe/Madrid (default: launch.timeZone, LYNKEUS_TIME_ZONE)

epoch.description: the instant the app’s clock starts at on a host the run starts, ISO 8601 or milliseconds (default: launch.epoch, LYNKEUS_EPOCH)

once.description: no second chance for a case that fails

out.description: write the run as a directory a report can read: run.json and cases.jsonl, a line per attempt

no_app_events.description: with --out: leave the app's own event list unread. Reading it can turn on the app's tracking debug, which may draw on the screen; frames two runs compare should not have it

screenshots.description: with --out: a frame of the screen after every step of the app

video.description: with --out: film each case, where the host films (the step says at what second it began)

traces.description: listen for the backend’s OpenTelemetry traces (OTLP over HTTP) and keep, under each step, what the backend did for it; point the backend’s OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT at http://localhost:<traces-port>

push.description: with --out: upload the run to the reports service and print the report’s address; the report is made when the run starts and fills case by case

jobs.description: cases at once, each on its own host (needs --ports) (default 1)

ports.description: the driver port of each job, comma-separated: where its host dials in

host_command.description: starts a fresh host for every case and stops it after; {port} is where the host dials, {job} the job

keep_hosts.description: with --host-command: start each job’s host once and keep it for the job’s cases, starting it again when it exits, its app stops answering or its heap passes --host-heap percent

host_timeout.description: with --keep-hosts: how long a host may take to attach (it builds the app first) (default 600000)

in_order.description: with --jobs: take the cases in the order given, not the longest first

dry_run.description: parse and list the steps without running them

mcp/tool/case_status.name: case_status
mcp/tool/case_status.description:
Where a run of cases is: how many are done, what each job is running and in which section, and the time left

Where a case run stands: cases done, what each job runs and in which section, failures so far and the time left. Give the run's out directory, or nothing for the project's last run. Call it while case_run runs (from here or from a terminal) to follow a long suite.

dir.description: the run directory (case run --out), or its progress.ndjson; default: the last run here

mcp/tool/fastsim_install.name: fastsim_install
mcp/tool/fastsim_install.description:
Download Lynkeus FastSim for this machine and a platform from lynkeus.io with the organization's key

Downloads Lynkeus FastSim (the fast simulator; optional and paid, part of the Team plan, plans at https://lynkeus.io/pricing) for this machine and the platform asked for, and answers where it went. Needs the sign-in the person saved by running lynkeus login in a terminal (a browser step an agent cannot do: when there is none, tell the person to run it), or else, for CI, LYNKEUS_CLOUD_KEY in this server's environment (an API key an owner of the organization made with “May download Lynkeus FastSim”; other keys are refused with that message). Then read the README.md in that folder: it says how to bundle the app and run case_run with host_command on it. Call it when the person asks for Lynkeus FastSim or their organization has it; otherwise the headless host and the Simulator or emulator are free and cover the same cases. variant.description: a build by name instead of this machine's (darwin-arm64-ios, linux-x64-android)

no_browser.description: when a sign-in is needed, print its address instead of opening it

Why the last thing failed: screen, requests and trace read as rules

Runs by itself after a failed step.

Lynkeus — drive a React Native app from the outside, through the agent inside it

Drive — the app that is running, through the agent inside it

                                               Route, path and every element on screen, in ms
  press <target> [--in <target>] [--nth <n>] [--hold <ms>] [--js] [--settle]
                                               A finger on an element
  type <text> [target] [--in <target>] [--nth <n>] [--paste] [--submit] [--clear]
                                               Type into the focused input, or tap a target first

  nav <route> [params]                         Jump straight to a route (a teleport, not a user action)

  os language [tag]                            Simulator: relaunch the app in a locale
